subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the canonical distributed runtime architecture track, narrow it to a Phase 0/1 per-agent lifecycle milestone, or defer it behind the subagent execution-backend work?
rationale: The requested split changes core runtime ownership, security boundaries, config/protocol surfaces, and deployment modes, which cannot be safely selected by cleanup automation.

options.title: Keep canonical RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella architecture decision and let narrower PRs such as worker isolation or execution placement link back to it.

options.title: Narrow to Phase 0/1
options.body: Retitle or scope the issue to per-agent lifecycle and local-split behavior first, leaving distributed/container orchestration to follow-up issues.

options.title: Defer behind backend placement
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 the active design center and leave this issue parked until that surface proves the missing runtime API.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella architecture decision and let narrower PRs such as worker isolation or execution placement link back to it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from current agent-runtime refactor history and the open worker-runtime isolation PR.
